observedBehaviour: Padding is how content gets room inside a rectangle on both rectangular surfaces, and only the flow one grows with what it holds. A SECTION carrying its own fill is content-driven: copy 34.8 pt tall with padding(12) lays out 58.8 pt tall (content + padding) and wraps at 266.71 pt inside a 290.71 pt section, the width less the padding. softPanel(color, 8, 12) measures identically — fill, corner radius and padding in one call, still content-sized — so ROUNDED CORNERS ARE NOT A REASON TO LEAVE THE FLOW BUILDER. A SHAPE CONTAINER is a fixed box: padding(...) does inset an anchored child per side (padding(top 6, left 24) moves a topLeft child 24 pt right and 6 pt down) and grows the box by the full padding outside the declared rectangle (rectangle(200, 40).padding(12) lays out 224 x 64), but content never stretches it — an 80 pt child leaves a 40 pt box at 40 and overflows, and a paragraph inside wraps at 199 pt rather than at the 176 pt the horizontal padding implies.

minimalReproduction.arrangement: Three identical 200 x 40 rectangles holding the same 60 x 10 spacer at topLeft, differing only in padding (none, uniform 12, asymmetric top 6 / left 24); then five content-sizing cases: the same rectangle holding an 80 pt spacer bare and padded, the same rectangle holding a wrapping paragraph, a section with fillColor and padding(12) holding that paragraph, and a section with softPanel(colour, 8, 12) holding it. Compare each child's offset from its container's origin, each container's laid-out size against the declared one, and each container's height against its content.

workaround: Use padding for the space inside a rectangle — it is the property that owns children inside their owner, and one value replaces an offset repeated on every child. For a card or panel under content of unknown height, put it on the flow builder: softPanel(colour, radius, padding), or fillColor + cornerRadius + padding when the parts come from different tokens. Reach for a shape container when the surface is a shape a rectangle cannot express (circle, chevron, SVG path) or a deliberately fixed band with layered children; there the author owns the size — declare it smaller by the padding and give inner copy an explicit wrap width.

sourceRun.note: Found by asking why no generated template uses shape padding: 38 shape containers across the corpus, none with a real padding, 8 explicitly zeroing it, and anchored children placed by position(dx, dy) 49 times against 30 bare anchors. The shapes skill never mentioned padding, and backgrounds-and-panels sent every rounded card to a shape container, which is the fixed box — so the gutter was written as a per-child offset in the one primitive that will not size itself.
